items.title: Weighted convexity forces equality of the two parameters with arbitrary positive weights
items.source_title: Schweitzer Miklós Matematikai Emlékverseny 2025 — Feladatsor és megoldások
items.author_responsibility: The selected statement and solution are the original Hungarian report. The proposer credits are printed on p1; the published solution text is unsigned.
items.material_provenance: Fixed original source PDFs with exact numbered block and source context.
items.difficulty_reason: The author pairs the two orientations of a nonconvexity witness to force convexity, then uses a blow-up modification of the arbitrary weight at the countable nondifferentiability set and a Blumberg dense continuity restriction. Opposite one-sided quotients at a nonzero derivative force equality of parameters.

dedup.scope: The current SQL has no matching row by Blumberg, Bajraktarević, Páles or weighted/Wright convexity. Maksa–Páles 2010 §3 is adjacent and its proof of equality differentiates at a point with local regularity; Problem 9 assumes arbitrary positive p and lower semicontinuous nonconstant f. Páles's 2009 conference abstract mentions removing regularity by Blumberg but supplies no proof or exact same quantifiers.

readability.basis: Full printed statement and selected author solution in the fixed annual report. Original Hungarian statement sheet separately cross-checked.

source_caveats: The printed definitions p*(t_k)=k and p*|S continuous imply local boundedness on S at u. A sufficiently small interval therefore avoids the finitely many exceptional t_k allowed by the bound. This is the reason the historical neighborhood hold does not persist.
The original quotient display on p12 contains a subscript inconsistency (v versus v_n). Preserve the PDF; the sequence and one-sided limits are explicit.
